terms: Kinlume is a community-resource prototype. It helps people discover assistance, plan possible visits, and coordinate item donations. It is not an emergency service, government agency, or a guarantee of assistance. These draft terms describe the prototype and its intended use; operator and contact information have not been finalized.

Directory records, hours, photos, eligibility information, and map positions can be incomplete or outdated. Confirm details directly with the organization before travelling. Recommendations do not establish eligibility, reserve supplies, make appointments, or arrange transportation. Estimated travel times are not live routes or transit schedules.

The assistant uses a third-party AI service with selected resource facts. Responses can contain mistakes. Do not rely on it for emergency response or professional medical, legal, or financial decisions. Do not enter identity documents, Social Security numbers, bank details, passwords, or other people’s private information.

Use accurate information, protect your password, and manage only organizations you are authorized to represent. Do not impersonate a nonprofit, publish fraudulent requests, post unlawful or abusive content, scrape personal information, or try to bypass security or ownership checks. Hosted accounts use Supabase email confirmation when enabled. A password-recovery interface and a parental-consent process are not implemented. Do not create accounts for children under 13.

Organization managers are responsible for the accuracy of their own listings, contact details, services, and supply requests, and for having permission to publish supplied content. A listing does not mean Kinlume independently verified or endorsed an organization. Imported directory records remain subject to their original sources and cannot be edited by an arbitrary Kinlume account.

A pledge expresses an intention to give items; it is not confirmation of delivery. Only the receiving organization records received items. Coordinate acceptance and drop-off directly with the organization. Kinlume does not process money, transport donations, issue tax receipts, or guarantee fulfillment.

Original Kinlume app content and code remain subject to their owners’ rights. Directory records, maps, photos, libraries, and linked websites retain their own ownership, licenses, and terms. Third-party names and logos do not imply partnership or endorsement. Users retain ownership of content they submit and allow it to be stored and displayed as needed to operate their listings and donation requests.

The prototype may change or be unavailable. External providers may fail or limit requests. Current local storage is not a public hosting or backup service. No promise of uninterrupted operation, current inventory, or a successful visit is made. Any future finalized terms must accurately describe the deployed service; changes will be identified by an updated date.

Public operator and contact details are intentionally blank while this is a private prototype. A working contact method and reviewed terms must be added before inviting public account registrations. No registered-company or registered-trademark status is claimed.
privacy: Scope and current status

This draft describes Kinlume’s current implementation. The hosted version uses Vercel for the interface and API functions, and Supabase for PostgreSQL database storage and authentication. Local development retains a separate SQLite database. Operator and public contact information are intentionally blank and must be completed before public registration.
Information you provide

Accounts use an email address and password. Supabase manages hosted account passwords; local development stores salted password hashes. The interface does not display readable passwords. Your survey can contain your purpose, preferred name, assistance needs, search area, travel and accessibility preferences, optional household range and circumstances, and optional notes. Organization managers submit public organization and resource information. Donors submit item quantities; the app stores pledges and delivery records.
How information is used

Account information supports sign-in and ownership checks. Private survey answers seed searches and visit preferences. Organization records support public listings and donation requests. Pledge and delivery records support accurate totals. Organizations do not receive your private questionnaire through their dashboard. Only provide information needed for these functions.
AI messages and personalization

Chat messages, recent conversation context, selected resource facts, and visit preferences you explicitly discuss are sent through the server to the configured AI provider, currently Groq. If you opt in to saved-profile personalization, selected needs and travel preferences are included. Your name, account email, and private notes are excluded from automatic profile context. Anything you type into chat is part of that message, including sensitive details you choose to include. Provider processing and retention are governed by the provider’s terms; Kinlume does not promise zero provider retention.
Directory, location, map and photo services

Location and resource-type searches may be sent to Feed America (feedam.org), Give Food, Photon, or OpenStreetMap-related query providers depending on the region and available data. Resource names and locations may be sent to Wikimedia Commons to find licensed photos. Your browser requests map tiles and images from their servers, which can receive your IP address and ordinary request information. Selecting current location asks the browser for permission; map coordinates are processed in the current page rather than saved in your questionnaire automatically. Following directions, contact, source, or other external links shares ordinary browser request information with that destination.
What is public and what is private

Published organization/resource listings and supply requests are visible to other app users. Organization owners can review relevant pledge quantities and delivery records. Private surveys are account-owned. Do not put private personal information into public organization names, descriptions, addresses, requests, or uploaded listing content.
Cookies and device storage

Hosted sign-in uses Secure, HttpOnly access and refresh cookies. Access tokens last up to one hour; the browser refresh cookie lasts up to seven days unless you sign out. Supabase’s configured server-side session rules also apply. Local development uses a separate seven-day session cookie. Browser localStorage keeps saved resource IDs and snapshots, your last search area, text-size preference, and any earlier device-only donation records. Saved places are not currently synced through your account. Chat transcripts and individual visit plans stay in the current React page session and are lost on reload. Clearing browser storage removes device records but does not delete server-side account records.
Retention and controls

Accounts, surveys, organization records, pledges, and deliveries remain in the selected server database; automatic account deletion and a retention schedule are not implemented. Supabase manages hosted session records; expired local sessions are removed when a new session is created. You can edit preferences, disable saved-profile AI personalization, sign out, unsave places, and cancel eligible outstanding pledges. There is no self-service account export/deletion workflow or public contact channel yet. Those controls and a practical request process must be finalized before public launch.
Security and technical records

The app uses password hashing, server-side session checks, and organization ownership checks. These measures do not guarantee security. Application code does not intentionally log chat text, questionnaire answers, or API keys; provider error codes and routine server diagnostics may be logged. Hosting and external services may collect additional technical records under their own policies. Public hosting requires HTTPS, production access controls, and backups. Vercel and Supabase process infrastructure requests and authentication/database records under their own policies. Shared API limits use a hashed network-address bucket with short-lived counters.
Advertising, children and policy changes

The current app code includes no advertising or analytics SDK and no feature for selling personal information. Third-party services still have their own practices. The prototype is not designed for children under 13 and has no parental-consent system; do not submit children’s identifying details. This is not a claim of universal legal compliance. Update this notice when data practices change, and complete the operator, contact and request process before public registration.
